title: Taylor Swift
tagline: Every Taylor Swift album and song, who co-wrote what, every Grammy and AMA, and all six tours down to each Eras Tour show.
about: Every Taylor Swift album and song, who co-wrote what, every Grammy and AMA, and all six tours down to each Eras Tour show.

tables.name: albums
tables.label: Albums
tables.description: 12 studio albums plus the 4 "Taylor's Version" re-recordings.

tables.name: awards
tables.label: Awards
tables.description: Grammys, AMAs, VMAs and more, won or nominated (Wikidata's recorded history; not exhaustive).

tables.name: credits
tables.label: Songwriting credits
tables.description: Who wrote each song (bridge between songs and people). Producer credits are not included.

tables.name: easter_eggs
tables.label: Easter eggs
tables.description: Documented hidden clues, callbacks and behind-the-scenes facts, in our own words, each cited to its source.

tables.name: people
tables.label: People
tables.description: Songwriters credited on Taylor Swift's songs (from MusicBrainz work credits).

tables.name: songs
tables.label: Songs
tables.description: Every track on those 16 albums (title, length, position); no lyrics.

tables.name: tour_shows
tables.label: Tour dates
tables.description: Every Eras Tour show (date, city, venue, attendance). Earlier tours only have totals in the tours table.

columns.name: date
columns.label: Date
columns.description: As printed on the source table: a month and day with no year (e.g. "March 17"), so it is not a real ISO date and is never offered as a time axis or a year/date filter.

tables.name: tours
tables.label: Tours
tables.description: Taylor Swift's six headlining concert tours, 2009-2024.

metrics.label: Awards won
metrics.sql: SUM(CASE WHEN awards.result = 'won' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)

metrics.label: Nominations
metrics.sql: SUM(CASE WHEN awards.result = 'nominated' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)

rules: Only the Eras Tour has per-show rows in tour_shows (149 shows); the five earlier tours (Fearless Tour through Reputation Stadium Tour) only have tour-level totals in the tours table.

tour_shows.attendance sometimes repeats one combined figure across every night of a multi-night run at the same venue, when the source only reported a combined total (e.g. Wembley's eight nights). Summing tour_shows.attendance for a tour will overcount; use tours.attendance for a tour's real total.
credits only covers songwriting (writer/composer/lyricist), from MusicBrainz work credits; producer credits are not included.
is_single reflects MusicBrainz single and promotional-single release-groups, which includes some vault-track radio pushes alongside proper singles.
album_type is 'studio' for an original album and 're-recording' for a "Taylor's Version" release; is_taylors_version = 1 marks the same four re-recordings.
No lyrics are stored anywhere in this dataset, only song titles and short factual descriptions.

awards has no foreign key to any other table (an award isn't reliably tied to one album or song row), so its own columns (ceremony, category, result) can only be filtered or grouped through direct SQL today, not through natural-language questions - the planner currently only offers filter values and group-by dimensions from tables that join to something else.

tour_shows.date is the source table's own text (a month and day, no year - e.g. "March 17") and is not resolvable to a real calendar date, so it is stored as plain text rather than a date column; use tours.start_date/end_date for a real date range.
